description: List and heading labels: counters per list instance, restarts, skipped levels, templates, formats, legal numbering, lists across regions and tables, headings numbered by styles.
format: Each case is one document. Its defs are, in this order: a settings node with the attributes of the file's `settings` and then the case's `settings`; the file's `styles` and then the case's `styles` (a case style replaces a file style with the same identifier); the file's `numberings` and then the case's; and the page setup `ps1` with every attribute at its default. Then come the case's `stories`, then a body with page setup `ps1` and the case's `body`. Every such document is valid (model.validate) unless the case says `"valid": false`. `expected` lists, for each kind it names, every label of that kind in the document: `lists` by paragraph id; `sequences` by the id of the block holding the `seq` fields (paragraph, figure or footnote), one text per field in order; `equations` by equation block id; `footnotes` by footnote id; `references` as the text a `ref` field with that target prints (null: no label).

cases.description: Three items at level 0 count 1, 2, 3.
A deeper level restarts after every item at a higher level (restartAfter null).
A level that was skipped is counted once, at its start, as Word does: level 0 then level 2 gives 1.1.1 (owner decision 238).
A skipped level whose start is 5 is counted once at 5; the next item is 6.
A skipped level whose start is 0 is counted once at 0; the next item is 1.
A template that names a level below its own prints no label, as in Word (owner decision 238); an item of the deeper level counts as usual.
A template that names a level the definition does not have prints no label, as in Word (owner decision 238).
Two list instances (listId) on one definition number independently, even when interleaved.
The items left after the first one was deleted keep their listId and number as one list from the start.
numberingRestart sets the item's own level; later items continue from it.

A restart at level 1 changes only level 1 and below; the higher level continues. The restart value stays the level's start, so the next restart of the level begins there too, as in Word (owner decision 238).
A list continues into a table cell and out of it again, in document order.
A list continues through a region; regions are not visible to numbering.
legal shows higher levels as decimals (1.1, not I.1); restartAfter 0 on level 2 keeps (c) running across level-1 items until the next level-0 item.
restartAfter at or above the level itself means the level never restarts.
Letters go a to z, then aa to zz, then aaa (Word's convention); upper case alike.
Roman numerals; thousands beyond three are written as repeated m, so 4000 is mmmm.
Letters and Roman numerals have no zero; a value of 0 prints nothing, as in Word (owner decision 238). A decimal list prints 0.
A bullet level prints its bulletChar (• when null) and still counts, so deeper levels restart.
A level of format none shows no number of its own, but its template may show higher levels.
Heading styles carry numbering with one listId, so headings form one list; a skipped level is counted once at its start (owner decision 238).
A style based on Heading1 inherits its numbering and joins its list; a paragraph's own numbering wins over its style's.
Word counts each numbering definition of a list on its own (owner decision 238): paragraphs on two definitions with one listId have separate counters, each in its own format.
A header story is numbered on its own, not as a continuation of the body.
